blocks.text: Within the ZSDK Admin Portal, certificates are primarily used for defined web servers. They are required to use Browser Access.
You can manage certificates (Configuration & Control > Certificate Management > Certificates) using the following actions:

blocks.item: Upload an existing web server certificate.
On the Certificates page, click Upload Server Certificate.
In the Upload Server Certificate drawer:
Name: Enter the name of the certificate.
Description: Enter the description of the certificate.
For Certificate, click Upload File and select the certificate file to upload.
The uploaded, signed certificate must include the following information:
A PEM file containing both the certificate and unencrypted private key
RSA format only
A certificate chain
Click Upload to save your uploaded certificate.
See image.
You can see the uploaded certificate on the Certificates page and select it when defining an application segment.
Create a certificate signing request (CSR) for a web server certificate.
On the Certificates page, click Create CSR.
In the Create CSR drawer:
Name: Enter the name of the CSR.
Description: Enter the description of the CSR.
Subject: Enter the subject's distinguished name for the certificate.
The common name does not need to be a wildcard domain.
Subject Alternate Name: Enter the subject's alternate name for the CSR. This allows the certificate to cover multiple hostnames (domains only). Click Add More to add more.
Click Create.
See image.
You can see the created certificate on the Certificates page and select it when defining an application segment.
Edit a certificate.
On the Certificates page, click the Edit icon next to the certificate you want to edit.
In the Edit Certificate drawer, edit the fields as needed.
Click Save.
See image.
Delete a certificate.
On the Certificates page, click the Delete icon next to the certificate you want to delete.
In the Warning window, select the checkbox.
Click Delete to delete the certificate.
See image.

blocks.text: When managing certificates, consider the following:

blocks.item: You can upload up to 1,000 certificates for web servers. To learn more, see Ranges & Limitations.
When defining an application segment and selecting a certificate:
If you define an application segment with Browser Access enabled and the certificate is signed by a public certificate authority (CA), then you must select HTTPS as the protocol.
If you define an application and the certificate is self-signed, then you must select HTTP as the protocol.
If ZSDK is unable to verify the chain of trust to the public CA, then you must select HTTP as the protocol.
